To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of GLUTs and MCTs in the olfaction system is highly stereotyped.
the expression and distribution of GLUTs and MCTs in the olfaction epithelia suggest a metabolic coupling between supporting cells and the Bowman's gland cells.
the olfactory epithelial cells exhibit a stereotypical pattern of expression for GLUT1, GLUT2, GLUT3, MCT1, MCT2, and MCT4.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the expression pattern and cellular localization of GLUT1, MCT1, GLUT3 and MCT2, which may be involved in the metabolic coupling between the ORNs, SCs, Bowman's gland cells and the vascular compartment.
the expression of transporters involved in cell-to-cell energy transfer in a polarized epithelium.
the expression and distribution of GLUTs and MCTs in the olactory epithelium, and the possible role of these transporters in the metabolism of this tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the olfactory system is an example of a metabolic coupling between cells, which may be crucial for the maintenance of the olfactory mucosal epithelium.
the olfactory mucous epithelium is a metabolically integrated unit.

the SCs of the olfactory mucosal epithelium are metabolically coupled to the Bowman's gland cells and that glucose and lactate may serve as possible metabolic fuels for the ORNs and the cilia of the SCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucose, which crosses the blood-mucosal barrier, is used as a metabolic fuel by the SCs, which in turn may export glucose and/or lactate to the mucus layer.
glucose, as well as lactate, are exchanged between ORNs and SCs and Bowman glands, which may play an important role in maintaining the normal functioning of ORNs.
glucose and lactate are transported from the Bowman's gland cells to the SCs, and then from SCs to ORNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the olfactory epithelial cells exhibit a stereotyped expression pattern of GLUTs and MCTs, which may reflect their functional interrelationships and the role of these transporters in cell-to-cell metabolic interactions.
the metabolic coupling between ORNs, SCs, and Bowman's gland is mediated by the differential expression and localization of GLUTs and MCTs.
the olfactory mucous is not only a mechanical protection, but also an active metabolic environment that is crucial for the function of the olfactory system.
